# `vl805` – VIA VL805 xHCI controller (`1106:3483`): its PCI configuration space

- Bus: `pci` (offset in the PCI function)
- Base: `0x00000000`
- Size: `0x1000`
- Carried by: [`pcie`](pcie.md)

Bus 1, device 0, function 0 behind the root complex, reached through `pcie` `EXT_CFG_DATA`. Reset values are the reference board's dump with the fields Linux had written (command, BAR0, MSI address / data, the PCIe control words) put back to power-on. Its xHCI registers are `xhci`.

Sources:

- measured (high): Raspberry Pi 4B d03115: `sudo od -Ax -tx1 -v /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:01:00.0/config`; `lspci -vvv`
- standard (high): PCI Local Bus 3.0 type-0 header; PCI Express Base 2.0 capability structure
- decompile (high): bootloader bus scan `0x000A7118` (`PCIe scan %08x:%08x`); start4 `XHCI_RESET` `0x3EDC61F4` refuses anything but `1106:3483`

Carried by [`pcie`](pcie.md):

Bus 1, device 0, function 0 behind the root complex; the configuration space is reached through `EXT_CFG_INDEX` / `EXT_CFG_DATA`.

- linux (high): `pcie-brcmstb.c` `brcm_pcie_map_conf()`: anything but the root bus goes through `PCIE_EXT_CFG_INDEX`
- decompile (high): bootloader bus scan `0x000A7118` (`PCIe scan %08x:%08x`) finds it at bus 1 device 0

## `VENDOR_ACCESS`

Offset `0x043` · access `rw` · 8 bits

Opens the vendor port (`VENDOR_INDEX` / `VENDOR_DATA`) while 1. The bootloader sets it before streaming the hub image and clears it after starting the MCU. start4's `XHCI_RESET` sets it twice, each time right after writing `0` to the command word and followed by a 5 ms wait, and clears it before it restores the command word a byte at a time with `0x146` ORed in.

Sources:

- trace (high): pinned bootloader: `0x01` at `0x000A6934` before the first index, `0x00` after the MCU words; pinned start4: `0x01` at `0x3EDC5DC8` and `0x3EDC5E34`, `0x00` at `0x3EDC5F9C`, then command bytes at `0x3EDC5FA2` / `0x3EDC5FAA`
- decompile (high): start4 `0x3EDC5DAC`..`0x3EDC5DD8` (`ldh` command, `sth 0`, `stb 1` to `+0x3F` of the command word, delay 5000); `0x3EDC5F96`..`0x3EDC5FB0` (`stb 0`, command `|= 0x146` written low byte then high byte)

## `VENDOR_INDEX`

Offset `0x078` · access `rw` · 32 bits

Vendor indirect port, index half. The bootloader and start4 stream the VL805's own firmware through the port and read it back to verify. Indices seen: `0x52000` + n, byte n of the hub image (written as the byte repeated in all four bytes of `VENDOR_DATA`; a verify pass writes each index again and compares the low byte); `0x51000` / `0x51004`, `0x4C` / `0x80` after the image is written and `0x48` / `0` after it is checked (start4 also writes `0x48` / `0` after first clearing the image to zeros); `0x30000`, the MCU image's bus address in 64-byte units, `((phys & 0x3FFFFFFF) | (RC_BAR2_CONFIG_LO & ~0xFFF)) >> 6 | RC_BAR2_CONFIG_HI << 26`; `0x30004`, byte 0 then byte 1 of `VENDOR_DATA` set to `1` and `0`; `0x3000C` `0x500`; `0x30008`, the upper half of `VENDOR_DATA` set to `0x1800`, then its byte 0 to `1`. The bootloader waits 4 ms after the `0x51000` pair each time; start4 waits 5 ms after opening the port, after clearing the image, after each `0x51000` pair but the last.

Sources:

- decompile (high): bootloader around `0x000B6CE0` (`HUB2.0 fail` at `0x000B6DF8` on a mismatch); start4 `0x3EDC5EF8` (`MCU FW: %x %x`)
- decompile (high): bootloader loader `0x000B6C94` (index/data helpers `0x000B6E24`, byte `0x000B6E44`, half `0x000B6E04`, verify read `0x000B6ED0`, waits `bl 0x000AA3AC` with 4000); start4 loader `0x3EDC5D8C` (helpers `0x3EDC61B0`, `0x3EDC61CA`, `0x3EDC6190`; waits `bl 0x3ED6504C` with 5000), which refuses a hub image over 12288 bytes or an MCU image over `0x20000`
- trace (high): pinned bootloader: 9446 index/data pairs from `0x52000`, a verify pass at `0x000B6ED4` / `0x000B6ED8`, `0x30000` `0x00FFC800` (window at bus 0); pinned start4 under Linux's `NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET`: a zero pass, the image pass, a verify pass at `0x3EDC5EA6`, `0x30000` `0x10FFC800` (window at `0x4_0000_0000`)

## `VENDOR_DATA`

Offset `0x07C` · access `rw` · 32 bits

Vendor indirect port, data half: reads back whatever the selected index holds. start4 follows every write here, and to `VENDOR_INDEX`, with a read of the function's first long; the bootloader reads each written word back.

Sources:

- decompile (high): bootloader around `0x000B6CE0`; start4 `0x3EDC5EF8`

## `PCIE_DEVCTL`

Offset `0x0CC` · access `rw` · 32 bits · reset `0x102810`

Device control (low half) / status (high half). Power-on `DevCtl` `0x2810` is the spec default: relaxed ordering, no snoop, `MaxReadReq` 512. `DevSta` keeps `AuxPwr`. Running, Linux had added the four error-reporting enables and `CorrErr` / `UnsupReq` had latched: `0x0019281F`.

Sources:

- measured (high): config dump `0xCC`; `lspci` `DevCtl` / `DevSta`
- standard (high): PCIe 2.0, 7.8.4: Device Control defaults

## `PCIE_LNKCAP`

Offset `0x0D0` · access `r` · 32 bits · reset `0x65C12`

Link capabilities: 5 GT/s x1, ASPM L0s and L1, clock power management.

Sources:

- measured (high): config dump `0xD0`; `lspci` `LnkCap: Port #0, Speed 5GT/s, Width x1, ASPM L0s L1`

## `PCIE_LNKCTL`

Offset `0x0D4` · access `rw` · 32 bits · reset `0x10120000`

Link control (low half) / status (high half). `LnkCtl` is zero at power-on; running, Linux had enabled ASPM, common clock and clock PM (`0x0143`). `LnkSta` `0x1012` is the trained link: 5 GT/s x1, slot clock.

Sources:

- measured (high): config dump `0xD4`; `lspci` `LnkCtl` / `LnkSta`
